title: Run vs pass
summary: How to tell a run play from a pass play, and what the blockers do on each.

steps.text: Every play is a run or a pass. On a run, the quarterback hands the ball to a runner, who carries it. Watch Inside Zone: the handoff, then the running back looks for a gap.
On a run, the linemen fire forward and push the defense. They are trying to move people and open a lane. Watch how the whole line steps right together.
On a pass, the quarterback drops back and throws to a receiver running a route. Watch Slant-Flat: the quarterback takes two steps back and throws quickly.
On a pass, the linemen do the opposite of a run. They step back and form a wall, called the pocket, to keep the rushers away from the quarterback. That is pass protection.
So watch the line. Linemen going forward means run. Linemen backing up means pass. Defenses read that too, which is why play action, a fake run, works so well.

quiz.prompt: On a run play, what do the offensive linemen do right after the snap?
choices: Step back and form a pocket
Fire forward and push the defense
quiz.explanation: On runs the line drives forward to open a lane.

quiz.prompt: On a pass play, what is the pocket?
choices: The wall of blockers protecting the quarterback
A pass to the running back
quiz.explanation: Linemen step back and form a pocket around the quarterback so he has time to throw.

quiz.prompt: Tap the player who ends up with the ball on this run play.
quiz.explanation: The running back takes the handoff and carries the ball.

quiz.prompt: You see the linemen backing up at the snap. What kind of play is it probably?
quiz.explanation: Linemen backing up means pass protection, so it is a pass.

choices: A fake handoff followed by a pass
quiz.explanation: The quarterback fakes a run to fool the defense, then throws.
